newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares rebound but lacking momentum.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares rebound but lacking momentum.

text.p: Austrian shares recovered lost ground to end in positive territory on Monday but market participants noted the reversal was on thin volume.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed up 2.27 points, or 0.19 percent, at 1,211.80. It had dipped to an intra-day low of 1,204.10 points in early trade.

"Buying interest emerged mid-session but, with the exception of VA Stahl, turnover was moderate," a trader said, adding that he expected the ATX to vacillate in a 1,200-1,220 points range over the next few days.
Steelmaker VA Stahl closed at a new life-high of 480 schillings, up 1.9 schillings. Earlier it had climbed to 495 schillings, driven by international demand.
"Towards the close the buying interest began to dry up and the sell orders came," said a trader.
Market participants forecast the 500 schillings level would prove difficult to crack for VA Stahl.
Overall 11 ATX shares ended higher, nine lower and one unchanged.
Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien was the day's biggest gainer, up 13 schillings, or 2.27 percent, at 586.5 schillings. Traders said the stock looked well established in an upward trend channel.
Papermaker Leykam was the leading decliner. Its shares eased 3.8 schillings, or 1.19 percent, to 314 schillings.
March ATX futures were 4.0 points up at 1,214. The broad-based Vienna bourse index firmed 2.27 points to 1,211.80. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 257
